sections.title: Managing AI Agents
sections.description: This is a course on managing AI systems that can act: agents that draft, decide, negotiate, and execute workflows across real business processes. Rather than treating AI as a generic productivity tool, we focus on the messy boundary where models are powerful but unreliable. Across lectures, labs, and competitive team exercises, students will learn what humans still add when “the model can do the task”: problem framing, domain judgment, evaluation and monitoring, guardrails, and creativity. You’ll build simple agents (using no-code tooling), stress-test them, and design safe and effective systems. By the end of the course, you will be able to (1) decide when an agent should be used—and when it shouldn’t, (2) design evaluations and red-teaming processes that reveal failure modes early, (3) implement practical guardrails, and (4) communicate risk/ROI tradeoffs. The final project requires teams to build a small agent for a chosen business use case and demonstrate how human judgment improves system design.
